scheme_name: Grant of Financial Assistance to the Poor Parents Having Only One Girl Child Who is Studying 8th to 10th Standard
description:
The scheme titled "Grant of Financial Assistance to the Poor Parents Having Only One Girl Child Who is Studying 8th to 10th Standard" was launched by the Government of India to promote education among girls and to support families with financial assistance.

This scheme was introduced in the year 2015 under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to provide financial support to families with a single girl child who is pursuing education in the 8th to 10th standard. 

The scheme aims to reduce the dropout rate among girls in these critical educational stages. 

The government has set a measurable target to increase the enrollment of girls in secondary education by 20 percent by the year 2025. 

The scheme provides a financial assistance amount of ₹3,000 per annum to eligible parents. 

This amount is intended to help cover educational expenses such as school fees, books, and other necessary materials. 

The financial assistance is disbursed directly to the bank account of the parent or guardian of the girl child. 

Eligibility criteria for this scheme include that the applicant must be a parent or guardian of a single girl child. 

The girl child must be studying in a recognized school in the 8th to 10th standard. 

The family’s annual income should not exceed ₹2 lakh. 

This income limit is determined based on the income certificate issued by the competent authority. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for the parents or guardians to apply for this scheme. 

The application process involves several steps that must be followed to ensure successful registration. 

First, the applicant must obtain the application form from the official website or the local government office. 

The application form must be filled out with accurate details regarding the applicant and the girl child. 

Required documents include the income certificate, a copy of the girl child’s school admission form, and the parent’s identity proof. 

Once the application form is completed and the documents are gathered, the applicant must submit them to the designated government office. 

The application can also be submitted online through the official portal set up by the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

After submission, the application will be verified by the concerned authorities. 

The verification process typically takes about 30 days. 

Once the application is approved, the financial assistance amount will be credited to the bank account provided in the application. 

Disbursement of funds occurs annually, with the first installment usually released in the month of April. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the academic year and the continued eligibility of the girl child. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

State governments also play a crucial role in the implementation of this scheme at the local level. 

Each state has its own designated department that oversees the application process and disbursement of funds. 

For queries or assistance, applicants can contact the local office of the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

The contact details for the Ministry can be found on their official website. 

The scheme has seen a positive response since its inception, with thousands of families benefiting from the financial assistance. 

As of 2023, it is estimated that over 1 lakh families have availed of this scheme. 

This initiative is part of a broader government effort to empower women and promote gender equality in education. 

The scheme aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals set by the United Nations, particularly Goal 4, which focuses on ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education. 

The government has also launched awareness campaigns to inform eligible families about the benefits of this scheme. 

These campaigns are conducted through various media channels, including television, radio, and social media platforms. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also aims to create a supportive environment for girls’ education. 

This includes promoting community awareness about the importance of educating girls and reducing societal biases against female education. 

The scheme has been praised for its targeted approach to supporting families with single girl children. 

It addresses the financial barriers that often prevent families from investing in their daughters’ education. 

Moreover, the scheme encourages families to prioritize education for girls, thereby contributing to a more educated workforce in the future. 

The government continuously monitors the progress of the scheme to ensure that it meets its objectives. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme and address any challenges faced during implementation. 

Overall, the "Grant of Financial Assistance to the Poor Parents Having Only One Girl Child Who is Studying 8th to 10th Standard" scheme represents a significant step towards promoting gender equality in education in India. 

It reflects the government's commitment to empowering girls and ensuring that they have equal opportunities for education and personal development. 

This scheme not only provides financial support but also fosters a cultural shift towards valuing girls’ education in society. 

As the scheme progresses, it is expected to have a lasting impact on the educational landscape for girls in India. 

The government aims to expand the reach of this scheme to ensure that more families can benefit from it in the coming years. 

In conclusion, this welfare scheme is a vital initiative that addresses the specific needs of families with single girl children. 

It provides essential financial assistance to support their education and encourages a more equitable society. 

The ongoing efforts to promote this scheme will help in achieving greater educational outcomes for girls across the country. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's dedication to improving the lives of women and girls in India.
